summary.headline: MRVL's post-earnings de-rating eases -- back-to-back up days (+1.11%, then +6.96%) push it back above the $217 thesis-reference level, downgraded RED->AMBER. A hot August jobs report (+162K vs +55K) lifted September rate-hike odds to ~58% and drove a broad, shallow pullback across the Dividend sleeve and the crypto complex (COIN -4.22%, MARA -2.42%, IBIT/ETHA -2.4-2.5%) -- no new company-specific bad news in either group. AI-infrastructure/semiconductor names bucked the tape (LRCX +5.12%, AMD +4.65%, CRDO +3.76%, TSM +2.79%) on continued strong results and guidance. HUT +6.17% decoupled from the crypto pullback on its AI data-center pivot. CWAN roster-integrity bug persists (~71st consecutive day; PRs #11/#12/#14 still open/unmerged), plus a newer EIX->PGY portfolios.json drift fixed on-branch but not yet merged to main.

flags.headline: Post-earnings de-rating easing; second straight up day, back above the thesis reference level
flags.detail: MRVL closed 9/4 at $223.41 (+6.96%), its best day in weeks, as part of a broader AI-infrastructure/semiconductor rally (LRCX +5.12%, AMD +4.65%, CRDO +3.76%, TSM +2.79%) rather than any new company-specific news -- coverage attributes the move to the market catching up to the already-reported Q2 beat and raised FY2028 guide (~$18B). This is the second consecutive up day (+1.11% on 9/3) after weeks of post-earnings de-rating. Price is now back above the $217 level the screener's own risk framing cited as a sensitivity marker, though still ~17.9% below the pre-earnings $272 high. Downgraded from RED to AMBER given the sustained recovery; not yet resolved to GREEN since the stock remains well below its high and the next dedicated catalyst (an analyst day) isn't until October.
flags.thesis_link: Matches MRVL key_risk: 'Forward P/E of 50.2x...the ~20% pullback from $272 to $217 after Q2 earnings...shows the market's sensitivity to execution risk.' Price has recovered back above that $217 reference point for the first time since the de-rating began.

evidence.source: Stock analysis / market commentary aggregating Q2 results and sector rally

flags.headline: Broad crypto-complex pullback: COIN -4.22%, MARA -2.42%, plus IBIT/ETHA -2.4-2.5% (portfolio, informational)
flags.detail: COIN (-4.22%), MARA (-2.42%), IBIT (-2.43%) and ETHA (-2.52%) all declined together on 9/4 with no distinct new company-specific catalyst for any of them -- consistent with a broad crypto-market/risk-off day rather than an idiosyncratic development. The hotter-than-expected August jobs report (+162K vs. +55K consensus) pushed implied odds of a September Fed rate move to ~58% and drove a modest broad equity pullback (SPY -0.38%); crypto-sensitive names moved more than the tape. COIN's move sits against its already-known standing risk (Q2 2026 revenue -19% YoY, prolonged crypto downturn); MARA's move sits against its already-known standing risk (leveraged BTC-price derivative, no news specific to MARA). HUT, by contrast, rallied +6.17% on its AI-data-center pivot (see GREEN note below), decoupling from the crypto-beta names.
flags.thesis_link: COIN matches key_risk: 'Prolonged crypto market downturn...Q2 2026 revenue declined 19% YoY.' MARA matches key_risk: 'Revenue concentration in bitcoin mining means financial performance remains a leveraged derivative of BTC price.' Neither risk is newly materializing today -- this reads as normal volatility within an already-flagged risk category, not a new development.

evidence.source: Bloomberg -- 'Stocks Fall as Jobs Fuel Bets Fed Will Raise Rates: Markets Wrap'

flags.headline: Hawkish August jobs report lifts September rate-hike odds to ~58%; broad, shallow pullback across Dividend/defensive names
flags.detail: August nonfarm payrolls came in at +162K vs. +55K consensus (unemployment steady at 4.1%), a decisively hot print that pushed futures-implied odds of a Fed rate hike at the Sept. 15-16 FOMC meeting to roughly 58% (from ~50% the prior day) -- notably a hike, not a cut, given the current hold at 3.50-3.75%. The Dow fell 0.51%, S&P 500 -0.38%, Nasdaq -0.29% on 9/4. The book's Dividend/defensive sleeve saw a broad, shallow pullback consistent with this: ORI -2.70%, ADP -2.13%, GD -1.75%, SYK -1.61%, STLD -1.57%, NTR -1.52%, DVN -1.49%, CL -1.43%, LMT -1.43%, SSNC -1.16%, NEE -0.77%, ATO -0.88%, DGX -0.88%. No single-name catalyst was found for any of these on top of the macro move (ORI: routine insider sale + ex-dividend, no new operational news; ADP: soft own-brand August payrolls print plus routine CEO 10b5-1 sale, no earnings news; GD: actually received a new $194M Navy contract mod, still traded down with the tape). Flagging as one portfolio-level macro flag rather than 13 separate line items -- this is a rate-sensitivity read on the sleeve, not a set of thesis-specific developments.

evidence.source: Bloomberg -- 'Stocks Fall as Jobs Fuel Bets Fed Will Raise Rates: Markets Wrap'

flags.headline: HUT +6.17%, decoupling from the crypto-complex pullback on its AI data-center pivot
flags.detail: Hut 8 rallied +6.17% to $93.50 even as COIN/MARA/IBIT/ETHA all declined on the same session -- continued follow-through on the late-August news of a reported ~$35B Nvidia/Anthropic-linked AI data center deal, plus a Needham reiterated Buy ($138 PT) and a Freedom Capital Markets Buy initiation. This is a positive read against HUT's own key_risk ('material AI data center revenue not expected until Q2 2027...12+ month execution gap') -- the market is pricing in that this deal narrows that gap, though the revenue itself has not yet arrived.
flags.thesis_link: Constructive relative to HUT key_risk: '...material AI data center revenue not expected until Q2 2027, creating a 12+ month execution gap.' Deal news, not yet revenue, but market-perceived as narrowing that gap.

evidence.source: TipRanks -- Hut 8 AI infrastructure pivot coverage
